blinded_validation_rationale: VCP already received the most rigorous validation in the program: an 82-case blinded gold-standard study (4 independent reviewer personas per case: Minervini-native, classical-TA, quant-literalist, adversarial false-positive-hunter), a frozen rubric (rubric_v2.md, with a 4th INSUFFICIENT_DATA identity state added specifically to stop reviewers guessing), Wilson-style 95% CIs on every precision/recall figure, and — critically — a Phase 3C revalidation that FROZE 11 specific predicted case-flips BEFORE the Trend Template fix shipped, then confirmed all 11/11 flipped exactly as predicted with zero unintended regressions on a full 82-case rerun (only 2 extra flips, both on already-unlabeled/ambiguous cases). That is a closed, evidence-complete loop for the question it was built to answer (does the Trend Template precondition fix the diagnosed defect). A fresh from-scratch review is NOT decision-critical right now. What remains open is narrower: (a) System D's post-fix precision is still only 28.6% (tp=2,fp=5,fn=6,tn=35) — a real, already-measured gap, not something a new review would newly discover; (b) two "second fix" candidates (case_0034 ADEA, case_0039 OMF — a sustained-prior-advance / orderliness-gap hypothesis) were explicitly parked as out-of-scope, n=2, not yet authorized. If that second-fix hypothesis is ever authorized, the existing infrastructure (candidate pool, blinding harness, adjudicate_and_compare.py, rubric_v2.md) can be reused directly against a small targeted sample — not rebuilt at N=82. Reflexively re-running an 80-case study on a family that just closed one would burn reviewer-hours the evidence does not call for.
canonical_geometry_requirement: VCP's geometry is a SEQUENCE, not a single shape: a future canonical schema needs an ordered list of contraction spans (each a {high: (t,price), low: (t,price), depth_pct, avg_volume} tuple, 2-6 of them), the pivot (the final contraction's high, as both a price level and an anchor point), the trend-continuation precondition state (a boolean plus the 150/200-day SMA values that produced it, since that precondition now independently gates both engines and is itself citable per-symbol evidence), and the base's top/floor as a horizontal band (for zone rendering) distinct from the entry/stop/target price-line trio System A already emits. Unlike a single-candle or MA-pullback pattern, VCP has no single "trigger bar" until the breakout candle itself — its geometry is inherently a multi-anchor polyline PLUS a still-open lifecycle state (forming vs. triggered vs. failed), so the schema must support an anchor list of variable length (2-6 points) rather than a fixed geometry shape, and must carry the lifecycle field that neither current implementation actually populates (System A hardcodes "ready"; System D is stateless). It should also carry a provenance path per contraction leg (which raw bars produced each high/low) so a chart overlay can highlight the exact candles the detector used, since today only System A exposes candidate anchors at all and even those are (t, price) points, not spans into the underlying bar array.

defect_class_findings.detail: vcp.py:795-797 (why_it_matters): 'Historically, VCPs with {n}+ contractions and a final tightening below 8% produce 25%+ moves within 8-12 weeks when they trigger cleanly on volume.' This is a specific, quantitative win-rate/return claim shown to paying users. The detector's own code computes no such statistic (no backtest, no historical outcome tracking anywhere in vcp.py), and the primary source this family is built on explicitly documents that no such figure exists: docs/superpowers/research/bases/03-minervini-vcp-powerplay.md:165-170 states 'measured_performance: none published... no win rate, no failure rate, no sample size, no period, and no base rate' -- the book's per-name outcomes (465%, 118%, 525%, 75%) are flagged there as survivorship-selected anecdotes, not a rate. Secondary, lower-stakes instance: vcp.py:778-787 attributes VCP-as-core-setup to 'Kristjan Kullamägi (Qullamaggie)' and a specific IBD/Ryan Pierpont framing with no citation anywhere in this repo's research corpus.

System A's _MAX_PATTERN_BARS=90 (vcp.py:78; docstring line 14-15 says 'Window: 30-90 bars (typically 6-13 weeks)') hard-excludes any base longer than ~18 weeks -- but Minervini's own published worked examples run to 27 weeks (NFLX) and 40 weeks (VIVO) per docs/superpowers/research/bases/03-minervini-vcp-powerplay.md:159,235-236. The docstring's 'typically' framing is honest about the common case but the hard 90-bar gate silently refuses cases the primary source itself treats as canonical. System D (vcp_state) has no equivalent total-length cap -- VCP_MAX_AGE_BARS=60 (base_catalog.py:2653) only bounds recency of the last confirmed swing, a different quantity.

Two thresholds for the identical Minervini-sourced concept diverge between engines with no comment acknowledging it: (1) prior-advance floor -- System A _MIN_PRIOR_ADVANCE=0.20 (vcp.py:100) vs System D VCP_PRIOR_ADVANCE=0.30 (base_catalog.py:2622); Minervini's own text never states an example below 30% ('30, 40, 50 percent or even much more', research doc line 148-149), so System A's 20% is below both the primary source's own floor and its sibling engine's encoding of it -- unsourced-guess tier. (2) tightening ratio ceiling -- System A _TIGHTENING_RATIO_MAX=0.85 (vcp.py:98) vs System D VCP_RATIO_MAX=0.75 (base_catalog.py:2640), where 0.75 is explicitly DERIVED from the loosest of Minervini's 5 published worked-example ratios (research doc line 244-246, band 0.38-0.75). System A's 0.85 permits weaker tightening than any of Minervini's own five examples support -- unsourced-guess tier, no comment flags the divergence. By contrast, System D's Criterion block (base_catalog.py:2817-2987) tags every threshold PRIMARY_VERBATIM/DERIVED/OURS explicitly; System A has zero such classification anywhere -- every constant at vcp.py:76-101 is a bare number with a terse inline comment only.

System A's confidence FLOOR gates identity on a blended score that includes quality/context inputs, not pure geometry: 'if confidence < _CONFIDENCE_FLOOR: continue' (vcp.py:176-177, floor=50.0) where confidence = 0.40*geom + 0.25*vol + 0.20*ctx + 0.15*hist (vcp.py:173-174) -- so a geometrically genuine contraction sequence can be refused entirely (not merely scored lower) because context_score or volume_score dragged the composite under 50. Separately, `_hostile_context` (vcp.py:466-477, called at line 165-166) is a HARD identity gate (returns None, not a score) on the same three context fields (trend_stage/ma_alignment/rs_trend) that `_score_context` (vcp.py:602-616) ALSO uses as a 20%-weighted soft quality input -- the identical signals do double duty as both a pass/fail gate and a continuous score. The v2 gold-standard rubric (rubric_v2.md Questions 1-3) explicitly treats Identity/Quality/Lifecycle as three separate questions specifically to avoid this conflation. Note historical_score is a hardcoded constant 50.0 (vcp.py:171, docstring line 32 'historical_score: 50.0 (neutral prior)') -- 15% of the identity-gating floor is a placeholder that never varies.

types.py:143 defines Detection.status as Literal['forming','ready','triggered','completed','failed','expired'], but vcp.py:884 hardcodes 'ready' unconditionally on every emitted detection -- there is no code path that ever assigns any other value (confirmed this is engine-wide, not VCP-specific, via a grep across all 29+ pattern_engine/detectors/**/*.py files, all of which literal-string 'ready'). The gold-standard's own reviewer rubric independently requires 8 lifecycle states (EMERGING/DEVELOPING/MATURE/TRIGGERING/CONFIRMED/EXTENDED/FAILED/INVALIDATED/NOT_APPLICABLE, rubric_v2.md Question 3) and metrics.json's by_lifecycle breakdown proves this is a real, measured axis of quality (System A's precision/recall swing from 100%/40% on TRIGGERING cases to markedly different numbers elsewhere) -- so the code discards a distinction the evidence shows matters. System D (vcp_state, base_catalog.py:2714-2799) is architecturally stateless by family design (no persisted status field at all, per-call re-evaluation only) -- consistent with base_catalog's documented statelessness, not a defect unique to this Structure.

CLOSED CANONICAL SPLIT, characterized not relitigated per instructions. Two independently-maintained implementations answer different questions per the Phase-2C/3A decision (vcp.py:50-75 header, docs/uct-scanner-intelligence/decision-log.md): System D (base_catalog.vcp_state) is authoritative for WHETHER (screener base_matches + provenance panel), System A (detect_vcp) is authoritative for WHERE-TO-ENTER (pattern_detections, Compass tools find_patterns_on_ticker/scan_active_patterns). Different swing-detection primitives (System A: detect_pivots fractal window=3, vcp.py:112; System D: ctx.swings volatility-scaled zigzag segmenter, base_catalog.py:2724). Different output shapes: System A returns a scored Detection with confidence/narrative/geometry; System D returns a raw state dict {contractions,depths,depth,top,floor,prior_advance,bars,pivot} with no score, no narrative, no timestamps at all. Measured agreement: vcp.py header cites 3% (744-ticker sweep, 2026-08-31); the 82-case gold-standard set gives a different, more informative number since it's conditioned on cases either engine actually named -- engine_agreement.agreement_rate=0.39 (metrics.json: both_fired=7, both_rejected=25, disagree=50, n=82). As of Phase 3A+3C both engines now independently carry an equivalent Trend Template precondition (vcp.py:383-401; base_catalog.py:2671-2711), added separately citing the same primary source -- this narrows one prior disagreement without touching the WHETHER/WHERE boundary itself.

Fixture coverage (tests/fixtures/vcp/, 16 files) is reasonable on structural adversarial cases: already_broken.json (post-breakout), no_uptrend.json + rs_negative.json (hostile context), choppy_no_pattern.json, flat_data.json, expanding_contractions.json (not tightening), below_trend_template.json (Phase 3A's own regression case). NOT covered by any synthetic fixture: penny-stock/low-liquidity, corporate-action (split/reverse-split) artifacts, or extreme-volatility distortion -- confirmed by reading tests/fixtures/vcp/_generate.py (no split/penny/reverse_split token anywhere). Partially compensated by the real-production gold-standard's liquidity/volatility tier breakdown (metrics.json by_liquidity_tier: low_liquidity n=10 for System A, 0 false positives, 2 false negatives; by_volatility_tier: extreme_volatility n=8 for both engines, 0/0/8/0 -- zero fires either way, sample too thin to conclude whether that's correct suppression). A constructed read-only repro (throwaway script, scratchpad, not committed) built a declining penny-stock series (~$2, 260 bars, mild downward drift) then a 10x overnight reverse-split-style jump followed by a textbook 30%->15%->6% tightening sequence with drying volume: detect_vcp returned 0 detections on this construction -- did not fire on the one shape tested, most likely blocked by the Trend Template precondition (sma150 vs sma200 inequality) given the pre-split downward drift, though a differently-shaped split scenario (e.g. one riding on top of an already-uptrending stock into the split) was not tested and remains an open, unverified gap.

Two instances. (1) The narrative-layer claims flagged under D1 (25%+ moves; Kullamägi/Pierpont attribution) are uncited against this repo's own research corpus. (2) docs/uct-scanner-intelligence/decision-log.md documents only 'Phase 3A' (lines 13-125, dated 2026-09-02); it has NO Phase 3C entry, even though base_catalog.py's own code comments explicitly reference 'Phase 3C, 2026-09-03' twice (lines 2675, 2692) and a complete, evidence-backed Phase 3C revalidation exists on disk (docs/uct-scanner-intelligence/vcp_gold_standard/data/phase3c_predicted_flips.json + phase3c_revalidation.json, both populated and internally consistent). The decision-log's own stated purpose is cross-session continuity ('must remain recoverable across context/session changes', decision-log.md:3-4) -- it is currently stale relative to both the code and the evidence directory it exists to index. By contrast, every System D Criterion quote checked against docs/superpowers/research/bases/03-minervini-vcp-powerplay.md (base depth 10-35/40%, hard 60% cutoff, contraction count 2-6, Trend Template two-SMA conditions) matched verbatim -- System D's own citations are NOT stale.

System A returns real, usable anchor geometry: geometry.anchors is a list of {t,price} points (start_high, each contraction low, pivot high; vcp.py:734-742), pivot_ts (vcp.py:747-751), and geometry.extras carries n_contractions/contraction_pcts/pivot_price/last_contraction_low/pattern_bars plus structure_extras(c) (higher_low, aligned_ma, ma_distance_pct per the case_answer_key.json sample) -- genuinely chart-overlay-capable today. But it stores no per-criterion pass/fail trace: when detect_vcp rejects a candidate (six hard gates: recency, already-broken, prior-advance, volume-contraction, hostile-context, confidence-floor), NOTHING is recorded about which gate fired or the observed-vs-required values -- a caller sees only an empty list, with no way to answer 'how close did this come.' System D returns NO timestamps at all -- vcp_state's dict (base_catalog.py:2796-2799) has only prices (top, floor, pivot) and bar-count fields (bars), no (t) values anywhere, so it cannot drive a chart overlay without the caller separately re-deriving timestamps from ctx.bars/ctx.swings. System D's static Criterion objects (base_catalog.py:2817-2987) DO carry source/quote/confidence per criterion, but that provenance is attached to the STRUCTURE definition, not to any individual detection instance.

detector_action_evidence: Detection logic itself is validated: Phase 3A/3C's Trend Template precondition fix was proposed against a frozen, blinded 82-case gold-standard evidence set and then re-validated with 11/11 pre-registered predicted flips landing exactly as predicted plus zero unintended regressions on a full rerun (phase3c_revalidation.json targeted_summary + metrics_pre_fix/post_fix). Geometry is already rich enough for chart overlay on System A (anchors, pivot_ts, structured extras) -- so RETAIN_GEOMETRY_ENRICHMENT is not the leading need, and nothing in the evidence supports CORRECT_DETECTOR_LOGIC, CALIBRATE, or REPLACE for the detection math itself. The single highest-leverage, cleanly-scoped, well-evidenced defect is D1: vcp.py:795-797 states a specific 25%+/8-12-week performance figure that the family's own primary-source research file (docs/superpowers/research/bases/03-minervini-vcp-powerplay.md:165-170) explicitly documents does not exist in the source ('no win rate, no failure rate, no sample size, no period, no base rate'). That is a narrative/explanation-layer defect, not a detection-logic defect -- RETAIN_EXPLANATION_FIX names it precisely. RETAIN_ADD_TESTS (corporate-action/penny-stock fixtures, per D7) is a legitimate secondary companion action but lower-priority than the fabricated statistic shown to users today.

provenance_readiness: Two very different starting points on the same axis. System D (base_catalog.VCP Structure, base_catalog.py:2806-2987) already has a real, static Criterion system: each of the ~13 Criterion objects carries condition/value/quote/source_id/confidence, plus explicit missing/missing_kind fields for anything Minervini did not publish -- this is genuinely the reference implementation the task asked this family to characterize. But that provenance lives at the STRUCTURE-definition level, not the per-detection level: vcp_state (base_catalog.py:2714-2799) either returns a small aggregate state dict or None, with no per-criterion pass/fail trail for the specific symbol being evaluated -- when it returns None, nothing records which of its ~7 sequential checks (swing count, trend-template, contraction count, tightening ratio, depth bounds, volume direction, prior advance, recency/still-in-base) actually failed or what the observed value was. Retrofitting per-detection provenance here is architecturally cheap, since the Criterion objects that would anchor 'source' and 'operator' already exist -- the gap is purely in the runtime function's control flow (early-return discards its own reasoning). System A (pattern_engine.vcp, vcp.py) has NO Criterion system at all: every threshold (vcp.py:76-101) is a bare module-level constant with a one-line comment, no PRIMARY_VERBATIM/DERIVED/OURS tagging, and no source citation anywhere in the file. Its per-detection output is richer in one respect (quality_components gives 4 named aggregate subscores, vcp.py:871-876) but equally opaque on WHY a candidate was rejected -- the six hard gates (vcp.py:134-177) each silently `continue`/`return []` with no recorded reason. Neither engine's output carries an algorithm_version field; decision-log.md:112-119 confirms the repo has no per-detector version convention at all, only informal 'Phase N' comments in surrounding code -- so 'algorithm-version' provenance would need a new convention invented for the whole pattern-engine, not just VCP.
quantitative_metrics_summary: Overall (82 cases, 48 with a clean positive/negative consensus label, 34 excluded as ambiguous/unresolved): System A precision 0.40 (95% CI 0.168-0.687), recall 0.50 (CI 0.215-0.785), F1 0.444, FPR 0.15, FNR 0.5. System D (pre-fix baseline as measured in the 82-case set) precision 0.111 (CI 0.031-0.328), recall 0.25 (CI 0.071-0.591), F1 0.154, FPR 0.4, FNR 0.75. Post-Phase-3C-fix System D: precision 0.286, recall 0.25 (unchanged), F1 0.267, tp=2/fp=5/fn=6/tn=35 (metrics_post_fix in phase3c_revalidation.json). Engine agreement across all 82 cases: both_fired=7, both_rejected=25, disagree=50, agreement_rate=0.39. Targeted revalidation: 11/11 (100%) of the pre-registered predicted false-positive flips landed exactly as predicted, 0 unexpected true-positive flips, 2 extra unpredicted flips both on cases with no consensus label (system_d_only, ambiguous). Breakdowns also exist by lifecycle (8 states), liquidity tier (low/mid/high, n=15/32/35), volatility tier (normal/elevated/extreme, n=51/23/8), and agreement category (system_a_only/system_d_only/both_agree_positive/both_agree_negative) -- all with the same tp/fp/tn/fn/precision/recall/CI structure. Reviewer-agreement bookkeeping (unanimous=35, strong_majority=31, unresolved=16; consensus positive=8/negative=40/excluded_ambiguous=34) sums correctly to n=82 across every cross-tab checked.
geometry_readiness_rationale: System A (pattern-engine detect_vcp, the WHERE-to-enter surface) already emits genuinely chart-overlay-capable geometry today: an anchor list of real (t,price) points spanning start-high through each contraction low to the pivot, a parallel pivot_ts timestamp array, computed entry/stop/target price lines with named bases, and a geometry.extras block carrying n_contractions/contraction_pcts/pattern_bars/MA-interaction fields. That is visualizable with minor wiring, not a redesign -- hence GREEN rather than YELLOW. The gaps that keep it from a clean GREEN-plus are real but narrow: no zone polygon (derivable from existing fields), no lifecycle state (hardcoded 'ready'), and no per-criterion pass/fail trail on rejection. System D (vcp_state, the WHETHER surface) is architecturally much thinner for this purpose -- no timestamps at all in its return value -- but that is consistent with its role (a screener boolean/state check, not a chart-annotation source) rather than a defect; System A is the engine this family actually uses for geometry-bearing surfaces (Compass find_patterns_on_ticker / scan_active_patterns), which is what the color call is keyed to.
validation_card_markdown:
## Family Validation Card — VCP (Volatility Contraction Pattern)

**Role in this Tier-1 batch:** methodology/reference family. VCP is the ONLY family in this batch with a completed, blinded, gold-standard validation loop — use it to calibrate what "good validation evidence" looks like for the other six, not as a fresh target for re-derivation. ### Definition
Not a shape but a *property*: volatility (swing-range) must contract left-to-right through 2-6 pullbacks inside an existing advance, with volume receding, following a genuine prior advance (continuation, not a bottoming base). Source: `[TTLAC]` Section 6, verbatim throughout `docs/superpowers/research/bases/03-minervini-vcp-powerplay.md:131-216` (full-text-read primary source, page-caveat and transcription-caveat both documented). Minervini publishes NO numeric tolerance for "about half, plus or minus a reasonable amount" on the contraction-tightening ratio — System D's 0.35-0.75 band is explicitly tagged DERIVED (computed from his own 5 worked examples, not a quote); System A's equivalent (0.85 ceiling) carries no such tag and is looser than any of his own examples (see D3). Both engines now independently encode the Trend Template two-SMA precondition Minervini states is a prerequisite gate on the *trend*, not the base (Phase 3A for System A, Phase 3C for System D — see D6/D8).

### Detection Inputs
- **System A:** OHLCV bars, `detect_pivots(bars, window=3)` fractal pivots, and a `context` dict (`trend_stage`, `ma_alignment`, `rs_trend`, `volume_signature`, `regime`, `dcr_signature`/`recent_dcr_avg`, `can_slim_grade`/`can_slim_score`). `days_to_earnings` is present in the context shape (per fixture files) but never read by `detect_vcp`.
- **System D:** `ctx.bars` + `ctx.swings` (pre-computed volatility-scaled zigzag swings from the shared `bases` module) — no separate context dict; MA/trend-stage inputs are derived internally from `bars` (`_sma`) rather than passed in.

### Pattern Identity Conditions (hard gates)
System A (`detect_vcp`, `vcp.py:104-190`, in order): min 30 bars → Trend Template precondition → ≥3 pivots → per-candidate: recency (final low within 15 bars) → not-already-broken → prior advance ≥20% → volume contracts overall (final-segment avg < first-segment avg) → NOT hostile context (trend_stage==4 AND ma stacked_bearish AND rs down, all three) → confidence ≥ 50.0 floor. System D (`vcp_state`, `base_catalog.py:2714-2799`, in order): ≥3 swings → Trend Template precondition → ≥2 pullbacks → recency (≤60 bars since last pullback end) → longest tightening run (ratio 0.35-0.75 per step) ≥2 → hard depth <60% → depth in [10%,40%] → volume falls (last run-segment < first) → prior advance ≥30% over 120 bars → price still inside the base (floor ≤ close ≤ top).

### Quality Conditions (soft, score-only)
System A only: `geometry_score` (count/tightening/final-tightness/first-depth composite, `vcp.py:480-535`), `volume_score` (decline fraction/magnitude/vs-50-bar-avg, `vcp.py:538-599`), `context_score` (trend_stage/ma_alignment/rs_trend/volume_signature/DCR/CAN-SLIM additive bonuses, `vcp.py:602-616`), `historical_score` (constant 50.0, never computed). Weighted 0.40/0.25/0.20/0.15 into `confidence`. System D has no scoring layer at all — pure boolean/state, consistent with base_catalog's stateless-Structure design.

### Lifecycle Conditions
Neither engine implements a state machine. System A hardcodes `"status": "ready"` on every emission (`vcp.py:884`) despite the schema supporting 6 states (`types.py:143`) — engine-wide gap, not VCP-specific. System D is stateless by family design. The gold-standard's own reviewer rubric (`rubric_v2.md` Question 3) independently requires 8 lifecycle labels and `metrics.json`'s `by_lifecycle` breakdown proves the distinction predicts detector accuracy — a real gap between what the evidence shows matters and what the code tracks (see D5).

### Invalidators
Documented in the primary source and echoed in System A's narrative (not code-enforced as a post-hoc check — this is forward guidance text, not a monitored condition): close back below the last contraction low; a post-breakout close below the 20-day MA ("cuts success in about half" — Minervini's own relative, sample-free claim, correctly NOT presented by either engine as an absolute rate); three lower lows on rising volume post-breakout. System A's `failure_signal` narrative field states the first of these with a computed stop level; neither engine tracks invalidation as a state transition on an existing detection.

### Geometry Available / Missing
See `geometry_matrix_row`. Summary: System A is genuinely overlay-capable (anchors, pivot_ts, price levels, MA-interaction fields); System D returns no timestamps at all. Neither exposes a zone polygon, gap geometry, or a per-criterion provenance trail.

### Narrative/Explanation Summary
System A's five-field narrative (`headline`/`what_it_is`/`why_it_matters`/`what_to_watch_for`/`failure_signal`) is rich, paragraph-length, and mostly grounded in real computed values (pivot price, contraction percentages, stop distance) — **but contains one materially unsupported quantitative claim** ("25%+ moves within 8-12 weeks", `vcp.py:795-797`) that the family's own primary-source research explicitly documents does not exist (D1, P1). Two lower-stakes uncited attribution claims (Kullamägi, Ryan Pierpont/IBD) also appear with no citation in this repo's corpus. System D's Criterion `quote` fields, by contrast, verified verbatim against the research corpus with zero misquotes found.

### Confidence/Quality Scoring Summary
`confidence = round(0.40*geometry_score + 0.25*volume_score + 0.20*context_score + 0.15*historical_score, 2)`, floor 50.0 (`vcp.py:101,173-177`) — gates identity, not just display (D4). `historical_score` is a hardcoded constant (never varies), so 15% of the pass/fail threshold carries no information.

### Known Failure Modes (D7)
Fixture battery covers structural adversarial cases well (already-broken, hostile-context, non-tightening, flat/choppy). No fixture covers corporate-action artifacts, penny stocks, or extreme volatility. Real-production gold-standard tier breakdown partially compensates (low-liquidity n=15, extreme-volatility n=8 both fully clean of false positives in-sample, though the extreme-volatility cell has zero fires either direction on too few cases to be conclusive). One constructed reverse-split repro did not fire — inconclusive, not exhaustive.
